newsitem.title: USA: Changing view of MCI spurs share fall.
newsitem.headline: Changing view of MCI spurs share fall.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp stock continued its fall on Tuesday, and analysts said that a changing view of its role in a stock portfolio, and a tight arbitrage opportunity, may be partly to blame.
MCI was 1-1/8 down, at 29-5/8, at 1200 EST/1700 GMT, well adrift of a theoretical value based on British Telecommunications Plc American depositary shares.
"Previously MCI was a high growth U.S. long distance carrier," said Barry Sine of SBC Warburg. "Today if you buy MCI you are buying a call option on Britain's largest telephone company," he said.
Sine predicted that MCI would continue to have high turnover, reflecting a shift in its shareholder base.
"A lot of typical Nasdaq investors may get out," he said.
Bob Wilkes of Brown Brothers Harriman said the nature of the new company would be very different from the MCI of old.
"If it's going to be the same size as AT&T Corp, people will question what the growth rate can be," he said.
This is not to say that U.S. investors will not be interested in the new Concert Plc, but they will be different investors.
"You could make an argument that the Concert stock will be a better investment than either BT or MCI," said Bruce Thorp of PNC Investment Management and Research.
He said there should be a good home for the stock that combined the good yield of BT stock and the growth of MCI.
Arbitragers were the most skeptical about the deal's value given the nine to 12 month time to completion, and worries about regulatory approval.
"The spread is widening. There are a lot of sellers of MCI, people are getting out, taking their profits now," said one. "I am ignoring the deal," he added.
"It is going to take a year and there is going to be a lot of opportunities along the way to get in at more advantageous prices than these," the arbitrager said.
For arbitragers who were interested, it is a tough call because of the difficulty in borrowing the ADS shares of British Telecom to keep the short side of the deal.
"To arbitrage the deal, I have to buy MCI and short BTY. It is tight because people are not lending BTY stock," a second arbitraguer said.
The view will disappoint MCI, which told Reuters on Sunday that it specifically aimed to keep the U.S. shareholder base large and healthy.

Its two weapons to do this were the possibility, dangled in front of shareholders, of a 10 percent share buyback of Concert shares when the deal closes, and a heft investor relations presence in the U.S. to explain the new company. -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712
